findings.reason: The protected SQL solution calculates 3-month rolling averages of ride_distance and ride_duration for 2020 starting months 1 through 10. It uses a WITH RECURSIVE Months CTE (1 to 12) left joined to Rides and AcceptedRides to sum monthly distance and duration, then applies window function AVG(...) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING) rounded to 2 decimal places and filtered to month <= 10. The query runs in O(r + a) time and O(a) space; no candidate is required.
Monthly aggregation sum over 12-month spine combined with window function 3-row forward frame accurately computes rolling averages for 3-month windows starting months 1 through 10.
Scanning r rides and a accepted rides over 12 months takes O(r + a) time and O(a) auxiliary space for window aggregation buffers. Complexity evidence is bounded-domain certified and hash-bound.
Accepts Drivers, Rides, and AcceptedRides tables, returning 10 rows with columns month, average_ride_distance, and average_ride_duration.

The approach accurately details 12-month recursive CTE spine generation, monthly accepted ride distance/duration aggregation, 3-row window frame averaging, month <= 10 filtering, and O(r + a) time / O(a) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover 3-table self-join overhead, correlated 3-month subquery duplication, per-ride AVG miscalculation risks, rejected request exclusions, request date vs join date boundaries, non-2020 ride exclusions, empty month zero contributions, multiple ride monthly summation, and Nov/Dec contribution to Oct window.

App SQL and native SQL solutions both execute the identical 12-month CTE + monthly aggregation + window AVG framework with SHA-256 digests 3491ac5bd6121d54c631a8c3c758f6007da7b802563992022240502bfd931e30 and 59b920e2212c99e976dac6299c7fe8bfaedb99c94d45846febc67e14bfc863da.
